newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai insurer Ayudhya says sales to expand in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Thai insurer Ayudhya says sales to expand in 1997.

text.p: Despite a slowdown in the Thai economy and a sharp stock market fall, sales of Thai insurance firm Ayudhya Jardine CMG Life Assurance Plc are expected to grow in 1997, a senior executive of the firm said on Tuesday.
Veraphan Teepsuwan, chairman of the company, told a news conference that its board was pleased with the company's performance in 1996 and the firm was now strongly placed to meet future competition.
Veraphan did not make a forecast for the company's business this year.
The company quoted figures published this week by the Thai Life Assurance Association as showing that it was the fastest-growing life insurance company in Thailand during 1996.
Its share of the insurance market increased to 8.09 percent in 1996 from 4.75 percent in 1995, the company said, while its total sales grew by over 100 percent.

But the company suffered a total loss of 149.81 million baht ($5.76 million) during the first nine months in 1996 versus a profit of 123.43 million baht during the same period in 1995. During calendar 1995, net profit was 92.62 million baht.

"Rapid growth, combined with the falling stock market, led to a loss for the first three quarters of 1996. The SET (index) performed even worse in the last quarter of 1996," said Peter Fancke, president of Ayudhya Jardine.
"While we are disappointed with the SET's performance, we remain financially strong and expect healthy investment returns in future years," Fancke said.
The battered Thai stock index fell to a 56-month low last week.
Thailand's Bank of Ayudhya Plc and Australia's CMG Colonial Mutual Group each hold 35 percent of the shares in the company and the rest is offered on the Thai stock exchange.
Ayudhya Jardine shares closed at 87.50 baht each, up one baht, on Monday. There was no trading of the company's shares during the morning session on Tuesday.
